content.value_statement: Nested pattern matching can hide the main decision path in Rust code. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code suggest let chains for clearer Rust 2024 control flow.
actual_capabilities: Detects deeply nested if-let expressions with three or more levels.
Suggests Rust 2024 let chain refactors for Option and Result handling.
Combines pattern matches with boolean guard conditions when appropriate.
Checks that the project targets Rust 1.88 or newer and edition 2024.
Provides before-and-after guidance for cleaner control flow.
limitations: Requires Rust 1.88 or newer with edition 2024 for let chains.
Does not execute cargo, rustc, tests, or formatters by itself.
Cannot prove semantic equivalence without project-specific review.
May need adjustment when borrowing or ownership rules affect the refactor.

use_cases.title: Refactor Nested Option Handling
use_cases.description: Replace multiple nested Option checks with a shorter let chain while keeping fallback behavior clear.

use_cases.title: Review Pattern Matching Readability
use_cases.description: Identify control flow that is hard to scan and suggest modern Rust syntax where it fits.

use_cases.title: Modernize Rust 2024 Code
use_cases.description: Apply let chains to eligible code during an edition upgrade or cleanup pass.

prompt_templates.title: Find Basic Let Chain Opportunities
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Rust function for nested if-let expressions. Suggest a let chain only if it improves readability and the code targets Rust 2024.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Option and Result Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Scan this Rust module for nested Option or Result checks. Recommend let chain refactors and explain any cases that should stay unchanged.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate Guards and Pattern Matches
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these nested pattern matches and boolean guards. Propose Rust 2024 let chains where ordering, readability, and behavior remain clear.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare an Edition Upgrade Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Rust 2021 code for Rust 2024 let chain opportunities. Note version requirements, semantic risks, and tests that should verify the refactor.

output_examples.input: A function has three nested if-let statements to unwrap user, profile, and email values.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends a single let chain that checks each value in order and returns the email in the success branch.

output_examples.input: A processing function checks an optional value, validates it, then checks its size before doing work.
output_examples.output: The skill suggests combining the pattern match and guard conditions into one readable control-flow condition.

output_examples.input: A project uses an older Rust edition or version below the let chain requirement.
output_examples.output: The skill explains that the refactor should wait until the project supports Rust 1.88 and edition 2024.

best_practices: Confirm the Rust version and edition before applying let chains.
Keep let chains short enough that the success path remains easy to read.
Review ownership and borrowing changes after each refactor.
anti_patterns: Do not replace simple two-level checks when nesting is already clear.
Do not use let chains if they hide important error handling behavior.
Do not refactor without tests for branches that return early or fall through.

faq.question: What Rust version does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets Rust 1.88 or newer with edition 2024, where let chains are available.

faq.question: Does the skill run code or tests?
faq.answer: No. The skill only reads and searches files, then suggests refactors for review.

faq.question: Can it refactor Result handling?
faq.answer: Yes. It can suggest let chains for nested Result checks when the control flow remains clear.

faq.question: Will every nested if-let become a let chain?
faq.answer: No. The skill focuses on cases where let chains improve readability and preserve behavior.

faq.question: Does it support Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should reviewers check after using it?
faq.answer: Review fallback behavior, ownership changes, guard ordering, and test coverage for each affected branch.
